statements.claim: Krishna went into the forest alone, not with Balarama (Sangkarshana)
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 (Dutt): 'without being united with Sangkarshana, began to range alone in that charming forest'

statements.claim: He was dark as a rain-cloud, wore a crow's feather in his hair, and garlands of new kadamba and arjuna buds
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'dark-blue hue of the clouds of the rainy season', 'wearing a feather of crow', 'Garlands of new grown buds of Arjuna, Kadamba and Nipa flowers'

statements.claim: The forest was resonant with peacocks and low thunder among the hills, with plantain groves, new grass, lotuses and hidden fountains
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'resonant with the notes of peacocks', 'caves echoed with the muttering of clouds', 'adorned with plantain trees... new grown grass, twigs and lotuses', 'abounded in many fountains'

statements.claim: He used to stop under the great Bhandiraka fig tree, tall enough to brush half the sky, while cowherd boys amused him and he answered on his flute
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66: 'Beholding this Bhāndiraka fig-tree... traversed half of the sky'; 'the other cow-herds amused him with various wild plays... Krishna, too at times, played on his flute'

statements.claim: He came to the Yamuna bank, which was embellished with lilies and lotuses, swans and cranes, smooth landing-stairs, strong sweet current and many lakes
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 (vv.28-31): 'embellished with lilies and lotuses', 'resonant with the notes of swans, Karandavas and Sārasas', 'landing stairs were well-levelled and her water was sweet; she had many lakes and her current was strong'

statements.claim: Kaliya the serpent-king lived in a lake beside the Yamuna and his venom had made the water unfit to drink
statements.evidence: Index summary: 'Finding the Yamuna's lake poisoned by the serpent-king Kaliya'; excerpt: 'jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya'

statements.claim: Krishna quietly resolved: 'I should vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb the Kadamba tree, and jump into the lake, and vanquish Kaliya'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.66 excerpt (verbatim): 'I should, however, vanquish this king of serpents... I shall climb this Kadamba tree, jump into the lake and vanquish Kalya.'

notes: All setting details and the resolve are drawn directly from Harivamsha 1.66. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: The cowherds and cattle, distressed by the summer heat, came to the Yamuna and drank
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.47: 'gāvaś ca gopāś ca nidāghātapa-pīḍitāḥ' (cows and cowherds distressed by the heat of summer)

statements.claim: The poisoned water struck down their minds and they fell lifeless, as if by fate
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.48: 'viṣāmbhas tad upaspṛśya daivopahata-cetasaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'fall lifeless'

statements.claim: Krishna, master of all yoga and of the masters of yoga, restored them with a single nectar-showering glance
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.49-51: 'kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ... govindānugrahekṣitam'; pack excerpt: 'restores them with a single nectar-showering glance'

statements.claim: The cowherds rose from the water's edge with memory restored and knew it was Govinda's grace
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.50-51: 'te sampratīta-smṛtayaḥ samutthāya jalāntikāt / anvamaṃsata tad rājan govindānugrahekṣitam' (with restored memory they rose and deemed it Govinda's gracious look)

statements.claim: They were given back as if waking from a dreamless sleep, with no ordinary medicine involved
statements.evidence: Framing of the recovery scene consistent with the pack; no sourceable fact asserted

notes: Faithful rendering of BP 10.15.46-51; 'no one left standing to raise a cry' is consistent with all falling. No unsupported/contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna bound his cloth tightly, climbed the tall kadamba tree, slapped his arms and dived headlong into the poisoned pool
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.5: 'kṛṣṇaḥ kadambam adhiruhya tato 'ti-tuṅgam āsphoṭya gāḍha-raśano nyapatad viṣode'; Harivamsha 1.67: 'Tying his cloth firmly... emitting a leonine roar... jumped headlong down into the lake'

statements.claim: The water overflowed its banks like scattering clouds and the serpent's abode was shaken
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'The water thereof overflowed (on all sides) like scattering clouds. The huge abode of the serpent was shaken by that sound.'

statements.claim: The serpents rose with eyes red with anger, Kaliya at their head, dark as clouds with five hoods and a fiery face and tongue
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'serpents, with their eyes reddened with anger, rose up'; 'king of serpents Kālya... hue of clouds... five hoods, a fiery countenance and tongue and effulgent like the flames of fire'

statements.claim: The whole surface of the pool was covered by his burning hoods; the water boiled and the Yamuna fled in its opposite course
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'The entire lake was covered with his hood burning like fire... water there appeared as if boiling and the river Yamunā, stricken with fear, flew in her opposite course'

statements.claim: Kaliya loosed winds of fire; sparks and smoke poured from him and the great trees on the bank were consumed
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'powerful winds issue out of his mouth filled with the fire of anger. Scintiliations of fire, accompanied by smoke... All the huge trees... were in no time consumed'

statements.claim: His son Dara and his servant serpents rose with him, vomiting venom and flame
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'his son Dāra and his servants, the other leading serpents... vomitting the dreadful fire of venom accompanied by smokes'

statements.claim: Krishna sported in the water as if at play and was untouched by fire, venom and the serpent fury
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'sporting like a boy'; 'The powerful Krishna however did not die'

notes: The story stops before the coiling (correctly deferred to DKS_0073); variant_note about VP including the biting is respected. No issues.

statements.claim: Kaliya bit Krishna, the tender boy in yellow cloth with the Srivatsa mark, smiling face and lotus-soft feet, and wound his coils about him, holding him motionless
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.8: 'śrīvatsa-pīta-vasanaṃ smita-sundarāsyam... krīḍantam apratibhayaṃ kamalodarāṅghriṃ sandaśya marmasu ruṣā bhujayā cachāda'; v.9: 'nāga-bhoga-parivītam adṛṣṭa-ceṣṭam' (wrapped in the serpent's coils, motionless)

statements.claim: The cowherd boys on the bank, seeing him bound, were overcome with grief, terror and sorrow and dropped where they stood
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.9: 'tat-priya-sakhāḥ paśupā bhṛśārtāḥ... duḥkhānuśoka-bhaya-mūḍha-dhiyo nipetuḥ'

statements.claim: The cows, bulls and young calves lowed and cried out in their distress
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.10: 'gāvo vṛṣā vatsataryaḥ krandamānāḥ su-duḥkhitāḥ'

statements.claim: Three kinds of terrible omens appeared in Vraja, and the cowherds, led by Nanda, with children, old men and women, went out in fear
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.11-14: 'mahotpātās tri-vidhā hy ati-dāruṇāḥ'; 'gopā nanda-purogamāḥ'; 'ā-bāla-vṛddha-vanitāḥ sarve 'ṅga paśu-vṛttayaḥ'

statements.claim: Balarama went with them, seeing them so distressed
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.15: 'tāṃs tathā kātarān vīkṣya bhagavān mādhavo balaḥ'

statements.claim: They followed Krishna's footprints stamped with lotus, barley-grain, goad, thunderbolt and banner, and found him in the pool wrapped in the serpent's coils
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.16-18: 'sūcitayā padaiḥ'; 'abja-yavāṅkuśāśani-dhvajopapannāni padāni'; 'antar hrade bhujaga-bhoga-parītam... kṛṣṇaṃ nirīham upalabhya'

statements.claim: The gopis remembered his friendship, smile, looks and words, and saw the three worlds empty
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.19: 'tat-sauhṛda-smita-viloka-giraḥ smarantyaḥ... śūnyaṃ priya-vyatihṛtaṃ dadṛśus tri-lokam'

statements.claim: The gopis held up Yashoda, who had run after her child, shared her pain, told the old stories of Vraja with eyes fixed on Krishna's face, looking like the dead
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.20: 'kṛṣṇa-mātaram apatyam anupraviṣṭāṃ tulya-vyathāḥ samanugṛhya śucaḥ sravantyaḥ... vraja-priya-kathāḥ kathayantya āsan kṛṣṇānane 'rpita-dṛśo mṛtaka-pratīkāḥ'

notes: All beats of BP 10.16.8-20 rendered faithfully. 'Lived by Krishna as cattle live by grass' is a devotional gloss on paśu-vṛttayaḥ (living by cattle), connective.

statements.claim: Kaliya lay with his hoods crushed by the blows of Krishna's feet
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.30: 'pārṣṇi-prahāra-parirugna-phaṇātapatram' (hood-umbrella broken by heel-blows)

statements.claim: His wives came forward with loosened hair and slipping garments, children placed before them, and bowed with folded hands
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.30-31: 'ślathad-vasana-bhūṣaṇa-keśa-bandhāḥ'; 'puraskṛtārbhāḥ... kṛtāñjali-puṭāḥ'

statements.claim: They declared the punishment just, since Krishna's descent is to subdue the wicked, and that he looks with equal eyes even on his enemies' children
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.32: 'nyāyyo hi daṇḍaḥ kṛta-kilbiṣe 'smiṃs tavāvatāraḥ khala-nigrahāya / ripoḥ sutānām api tulya-dṛṣṭiḥ'

statements.claim: They said the punishment itself was grace, washing away the stain of the wicked
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.33: 'anugraho 'yaṃ bhavataḥ kṛto hi no daṇḍo 'satāṃ te khalu kalmaṣāpahaḥ'

statements.claim: They praised Krishna as the great Soul, storehouse of knowledge and wisdom, the Infinite One of unbroken power; Time, navel of time, witness of its parts; the Self behind elements, senses, breath, mind and heart
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.38-41: 'puruṣāya mahātmane... jñāna-vijñāna-nīdhaye... ananta-śaktaye / kālāya kāla-nābhāya kālāvayava-sākṣiṇe / bhūta-mātrendriya-prāṇa-mano-buddhy-āśayātmane'

statements.claim: They hailed him as the subtle, unchanging seer, source of scripture; homage to Krishna, Rama, son of Vasudeva; the lamp that lights the strands of the world and hides them
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.42-45: 'sūkṣmāya kūṭa-sthāya vipaścite... śāstra-yonaye / namaḥ kṛṣṇāya rāmāya vasudeva-sutāya ca / namo guṇa-pradīpāya guṇātma-cchādanāya ca'

statements.claim: His play lies beyond all that is made, yet through him everything made comes to be; though desiring nothing, he holds the powers of action and time; he knows the highest and lowest and oversees all
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.46-48: 'avyākṛta-vihārāya sarva-vyākṛta-siddhaye / parāvara-gati-jñāya sarvādhyakṣāya... guṇair anīho 'kṛta-kāla-śakti-dhṛk'

statements.claim: All beings of the three worlds — peaceful, restless, bewildered — are his forms; the peaceful are dear to him, and he came to guard them and uphold what is right
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.49: 'śāntā aśāntā uta mūḍha-yonayaḥ... śāntāḥ priyās te hy adhunāvituṃ satāṃ sthātuś ca te dharma-parīpsayehataḥ'

statements.claim: They pleaded that a wrong done once by a husband should be borne as one bears with one's own children, and that the serpent was giving up his life
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.50-51: 'aparādhaḥ sakṛd bhartrā soḍhavyaḥ sva-prajā-kṛtaḥ / anugṛhṇīṣva bhagavan prāṇāṃs tyajati pannagaḥ'

statements.claim: They asked Krishna to tell his servants what to do
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.52: 'vidhehi te kiṅkarīṇām anuṣṭheyaṃ tavājñayā'

notes: The praise-hymn and plea track BP 10.16.30-52 point by point. No issues.

statements.claim: Kaliya, regaining his senses and breath, slowly lifted his head and spoke to Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.54: 'pratilabdhendriya-prāṇaḥ kāliyaḥ śanakair harim'

statements.claim: Kaliya acknowledged the world was brought forth by Krishna, that serpents are fierce by birth, and that Krishna is the cause of everything, all-knowing, lord of the world
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.56-58: 'tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ... vayaṃ ca tatra... sarpā jāty-uru-manyavaḥ / bhavān hi kāraṇaṃ tatra sarva-jño jagad-īśvaraḥ'

statements.claim: Krishna spared him and ordered him to leave the water and go to the ocean with his wives and kin
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.67: 'O serpent, I do not wish to allow you to live in this water of Yamuna. Therefore repair to the ocean with your wife and kinsmen'; Vishnu Purana 5.7: 'Hari set the snake-king at liberty'

statements.claim: The marks of Krishna's feet on the serpent's heads would protect him from Garuda
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt summary (BP 10.16.53-67 rendered): 'declaring that the mark of Krishna's feet will protect him from Garuda'

statements.claim: Whoever remembered this command or bathed in that pool and offered water to the gods would be freed of sin
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.60-61: 'ya etat saṃsmaren martyas tubhyaṃ mad-anuśāsanam / yo 'smin snātvā mad-ākrīḍe devādīṃs tarpayej jalaiḥ'

statements.claim: Kaliya worshipped Krishna with divine garments, garlands and fine gems, honouring him whose banner is Garuda, then departed with wife, kin and sons to the island of the ocean
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.64-66: 'divyāmbara-sraṅ-maṇibhiḥ parārdhyair api bhūṣaṇaiḥ pūjayitvā jagan-nāthaṃ prasādya garuḍa-dhvajam / sa-kalatra-suhṛt-putro dvīpam abdher jagāma ha'

statements.claim: He went to Ramanaka island, the very island he had left before taking refuge in this pool
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.62: 'dvīpaṃ ramaṇakaṃ hitvā hradam etam upāśritaḥ'

statements.claim: The poison lifted, the Yamuna ran sweet again, and the cattle that had been perishing were restored
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.30 (Uddhava): 'vipannān viṣa-pānena nigṛhya bhujagādhipam utthāpyāpāyayad gāvas tat toyaṃ prakṛti-sthitam' (the cows perishing from the poisoned drink he restored, and made the water natural again)

statements.claim: Long afterward Uddhava remembered this among the wonders of Krishna's childhood
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.30, Uddhava's recollection; variant_notes: 'bpc1_035 is Uddhava's recollection'

notes: tradition_note correctly defers the dance-on-hoods to the previous episode per BP chronology. No issues.

statements.claim: A king listening to the tale asked how Kaliya came to live in the Yamuna, and the sage answered
statements.evidence: BP 10.17 opens with Śuka's narration (śrī-rājovāca at 10.16.67 closes the prior chapter); the question-and-answer frame is consistent with the text

statements.claim: The serpents owed Garuda a share, paid at every change of the moon
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.2: 'svaṃ svaṃ bhāgaṃ prayacchanti nāgāḥ parvaṇi parvaṇi'

statements.claim: Kaliya, son of Kadru, intoxicated with his venom's power, withheld the tribute
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.3: 'viṣa-vīrya-madāviṣṭaḥ kādraveyas tu kāliyaḥ'

statements.claim: Garuda, dear to the Lord, heard and was furious
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.4: 'tac chrutvā kupito rājan bhagavān bhagavat-priyaḥ'

statements.claim: Kaliya rose to meet him with many heads raised and venom as his weapon, but the son of Tarkshya struck him with his left wing shining like gold, and Kaliya was dazed
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.5-7: 'viṣāyudhaḥ pratyabhyayād utthita-naika-mastakaḥ / taṃ tārkṣya-putraḥ... pakṣeṇa savyena hiraṇya-rociṣā jaghāna kadru-sutam'; 'suparṇa-pakṣābhihataḥ kāliyo 'tīva vihvalaḥ'

statements.claim: Garuda is the vehicle of Vishnu (Madhusudana)
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.6: 'madhusūdanāsanaḥ' (seated on Madhusudana's vehicle)

statements.claim: Garuda once came to that spot wanting to eat a fish; the sage Saubhari saw the fish distressed when their king was slain and laid a curse: if Garuda entered that pool, his life would end
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.8-10: 'jala-caraṃ garuḍo bhakṣyam īpsitam / mīnān su-duḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā dīnān mīna-patau hate / atra praviśya garuḍo yadi matsyān sa khādati'; pack excerpt names Saubhari

statements.claim: Only Kaliya among the serpents knew this, and took refuge there
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.11: 'tat kāliyaḥ paraṃ veda nānyaḥ kaścana lelihaḥ'

notes: The sage who answers is Śuka, consistent with the framing; Saubhari named in the pack's excerpt summary. No issues.

statements.claim: Krishna emerged from the pool wearing a divine garland, fragrant and finely dressed
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.12: 'kṛṣṇaṃ hradād viniṣkrāntaṃ divya-srag-gandha-vāsasam'

statements.claim: Seeing him, all rose as though their breath had returned
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.13: 'upalabhyotthitāḥ sarve labdha-prāṇā ivāsavaḥ'

statements.claim: Yasoda, Rohini, Nanda, the gopis and the cowherds embraced him
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.14: 'yaśodā rohiṇī nando gopyo gopāś ca kaurava'

statements.claim: Balarama, embracing Krishna, laughed, knowing his power
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.15: 'rāmaś cācyutam āliṅgya jahāsāsyānubhāva-vit'

statements.claim: The brahmanas, elders with their families and wives, came to Nanda and asked him to give gifts to the twice-born for Krishna's deliverance
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.16-17: 'nandaṃ viprāḥ samāgatya guravaḥ sa-kalatrakāḥ / dehi dānaṃ dvi-jātīnāṃ kṛṣṇa-nirmukti-hetave'

statements.claim: Nanda gave cows and gold in thanksgiving
statements.evidence: Pack index summary and excerpt: 'Nanda gives cattle and gold to the brahmanas... bestows cows and gold upon the brahmanas'

statements.claim: Yasoda, the fortunate one who had lost and regained her child, held Krishna close
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.18: 'yaśodāpi mahā-bhāgā naṣṭa-labdha-prajā satī'

statements.claim: The river ran sweet behind them, the poison gone with the serpent
statements.evidence: Arc continuity: BP 10.16.67/3.2.30 (water restored to its natural state once Kaliya departed)

statements.claim: The village vigil: no one had seen the serpent go and none dared believe the boy would come back up
statements.evidence: Scene-setting atmosphere of the reunion; no sourceable fact asserted either way

notes: Opening vigil is connective atmosphere (pronoun 'him' refers to the serpent's unseen departure). All substantive claims supported by BP 10.17.12-18.
